evidence.quote: Zn-27 wt. % Al alloy (denoted as ZA27) belonging to the family of zinc alloys possesses good wear resistance, low-melting point, exceptional castability, super plasticity, easy machinability, and moderate strength compared with common cast aluminum alloys.
A total of 10 –40 vol. % Ti 3SiC2 reinforced ZA27 alloy composites were synthesized by hot pressing mechanically alloyed mixtures of Ti 3SiC2 and ZA27 powders.

The starting powders were mechanically alloyed (MAed) in a planetary mill (QM-3SP4; Nanjing Nanda Instrument Plant, Nanjing, China) for 3 h in steel containers under vacuum with a speed of 300 rpm, and a ball-to-powder weight ratio of 10:1.
The MAed powders were sieved with a /C080 mesh.
The MAed powders were ﬁrstly cold-compacted in a graphite die using a uniaxial pressure of 5 MPa,
then pressurelessly sintered at 870 °C for 60 min in Ar atmosphere with a heating rate of 30 °C/min
and hot-pressed at 430 °C for 90 min with a uniaxial pressure of 30 MPa in a hot pressing furnace (ZT-30-22y; Shanghai Chenhua Furnace Plant, Shanghai, China).

The increased hardness is attributed to the ﬁne-grained microstructure and the relatively hard Ti 3SiC2 particles, which act as barriers to the movement of dislocations within the matrix.
